sources.title: RIT MGMT-520 Circular Entrepreneurship course description
sources.author: Rochester Institute of Technology
sources.content: MGMT-520 studies creating new ventures based on circular-economy principles. It emphasizes circular-economy concepts, tools for circular opportunity recognition such as material flow analysis and life cycle assessment, and circular business models that generate environmental, consumer, and business value.

sources.title: Production in a Circular Economy
sources.author: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.content: NIST models circular production through five life-cycle activities: design product, acquire materials, produce product, use and consume, and treat at end of life. Circular product design uses data from downstream life-cycle stages to inform design. Closed-loop recovery covers reuse, repair, remanufacturing, and recycling, and requires coordination of activities, information, material flows, controls, and mechanisms across the system.

sources.title: NIST Circular Economy Program
sources.author: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.content: A circular economy aims to retain materials within the economy where they produce value and keep them out of landfills or the environment. Reusable, repairable, refurbishable, and recyclable product design can improve resource and economic efficiency, support new business models, and strengthen supply-chain resilience. Decisions require information about recoverable supply, material performance, processability, safety, and affordability.

sources.title: Circular Economy: A Product Life Cycle Perspective on Engineering and Manufacturing Practices
sources.author: Maya Reslan, Noah Last, Nehika Mathur, KC Morris, and Vincenzo Ferrero
sources.content: The NIST-led study frames circular economy at the system and product-life-cycle levels. It identifies the need for shared definitions, standard frameworks, and metrics for measuring circular-economy success. It also emphasizes that circular practices must be evaluated across the complete product life cycle instead of treating one activity in isolation.
